key_insight: Agreement across different LLMs about what COBOL code does can serve as a reference-free signal of summary correctness. The paper proposes using an LLM judge to assess semantic agreement rather than relying on wording overlap.
problem_solved: Estimating the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries when human-written reference summaries are unavailable.
method: Generate summaries under controlled conditions using diverse LLMs.
Use an LLM evaluator to compare pairs of summaries for semantic agreement.
Use inter-model agreement as evidence for confidence in summary correctness.
impact: This approach could help practitioners assess legacy-code summaries without costly reference annotation. Agreement is a confidence signal, not proof of correctness, because models can share errors.
visual_elements: Pipeline: COBOL code → multiple LLMs → generated summaries → LLM judge → confidence estimate.
Pairwise agreement matrix showing semantic consistency among model outputs.
Side-by-side summaries illustrating different wording with matching meaning.
Warning icon highlighting that shared agreement can still hide shared mistakes.
paper_title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
paper_authors: Marco Colombo, Balaji A Jayaram, Sowmyakumari Selvaraj, Sumit Tokkar, Animesh Kumar
